110	reference, settle it, and release only after that settlement is observed.

112	by the registration remains outstanding.

128	  not a shallow object-property scan;
129	- the mail waiter and its deadline timer were removed;
130	- repository, limiter-after-admission, token, mutation, mail and target hash work
131	  did not occur for the timed-out target beyond the already-ruled validation /
132	  pre-race work;
133	- admission counts are exactly one grant/one release for the target and drain
134	  reaches zero;
135	- no unhandled rejection or secret/address log appears.
136	
137	Add a separate deterministic started/deferred-KDF race test: make the password
138	KDF start and remain unresolved, force reservation rejection, assert the public
139	attempt may settle opaque but admission occupancy stays held and
140	`drainRegistrationAdmissions()` stays pending until the KDF is explicitly
141	settled, then assert exact one release and zero work/secret retention after
142	settlement. Do not use real time or a hostile KDF.

145	
146	The final M15 changed only `registrationAdmissionOccupancy().admitted` to
147	`pendingMailDispatches.size`; actual enforcement at `registration.ts:547-552`

152	so admission is derived from observed completion/pending-dispatch state instead
153	of the structural held counter. The exact gated 104th/no-work and burst tests must
154	fail with crisp intended assertions. The mutation must select tests, compile,
155	execute, fail for the intended capacity consequence, and restore exactly.

161	
162	`tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts:2892-2893` calculates
163	`queueDeadlineMarginMs` against the shared 18-second deadline even though every
164	admitted registration arms 28 seconds. Rework7 progress honestly disclosed this

---
name: agent-fleet-cli-setup
description: Where each agent CLI lives on this Mac and how to launch the Heartbeat fleet seats
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5b632377-be09-4278-a1e4-aa011d23f83c
  modified: 2026-08-03T19:46:27.209Z
---

Fleet CLI facts for DebateAIRO Heartbeat/Graph-Spine missions (verified 2026-08-03):

- **Codex CLI**: NOT on PATH; binary lives at `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex` (codex-cli 0.146.x). Non-interactive: `codex exec -c model='"gpt-5.6-sol"' -c sandbox_mode='"workspace-write"' "<prompt>"`. Its `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to `gpt-5.6-luna` — override per-invocation, don't edit config.
- **Hermes agent NOW RUNS QWEN and is slow (V, 2026-08-21)** — V struck the Hermes agent seat from the observability mission (board store only). `hermes kanban` works store-only without any model session: put `--board <slug>` BEFORE the action; ids are strings t_xxxxxxxx; `link parent child` = child waits on parent; in zsh pass flag pairs as arrays not scalar strings. Do NOT `boards switch` (global pointer shared with other missions).
- **Hermes CLI**: `~/.local/bin/hermes`, already configured model `gpt-5.6-sol` provider "OpenAI Codex" (OAuth). One-shot: `hermes --yolo -z "<prompt>"`.
- **Grok limit reached 2026-08-21** — decommissioned from observability mission (V order; opus reviewers only there). Ran a full REQ blind seat + docker-hatchet Router + accounts S3d greenlight that day.
- **Grok CLI**: `~/.grok/bin/grok`, default model `grok-4.5`. Headless: `grok -p "<prompt>" -m grok-4.5 --permission-mode bypassPermissions` (acceptEdits can hang on tool prompts in headless runs). Auth via `grok login` (only V can do this) — verified signed in and working on 2026-08-03 evening (WEIGHT-RESEARCH-R1 mission ran full research + review seats). No `grok auth status` subcommand exists; liveness-test with a tiny `-p` prompt instead (use `perl -e 'alarm 60; exec @ARGV'` since macOS lacks `timeout`).
- **Visible fleet terminals**: V authorized launching macOS Terminal windows via `osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script "..."'` (parity with their Windows Heartbeat setup). Write per-seat `run-<seat>.sh` scripts that tee to `logs/`, launch those.
- **Launcher content-readback is not optional** (learned the hard way 2026-08-22): the repo law says never sed-generate a launcher without reading it back — reading back SYNTAX is not enough. A sed rename that ran BEFORE the regex silently left a stale goal in place; zsh -n passed and the seat launched with instructions missing the ratified pin value. ALWAYS grep the built launcher for the specific values the goal must carry (hashes, session id, absence of stale phrases, non-ASCII residue) before osascript. Write launchers fresh from a heredoc rather than transforming the previous one.
- **codex exec resume can HANG ON EXIT after completing its work** (verified 2026-08-22): seat posted its full handoff to the Kanban ticket at 11:11 then sat at 0.0%% CPU for 81 min with no further output. Diagnose by reading the BOARD not the log — the log can lag the final board write. Cross-probe the relay with a tiny codex exec first; if it answers, the backend is fine and only that session is wedged. Killing it is safe once the handoff is durable; the session id stays resumable.
- **hermes --yolo -z BUFFERS stdout until completion** (verified 2026-08-21): a silent tee log is NOT a hang.     notify-unsubscribe  Remove a gateway subscription from a task

    context             Print the full context a worker sees for a task (title

    specify             Flesh out a triage-column task into a concrete spec

    decompose           Decompose a triage-column task into a graph of child

                        auxiliary.kanban_decomposer.

content.content:
usage: hermes kanban [-h] [--board <slug>]
                     {init,boards,create,swarm,list,ls,show,assign,reclaim,reassign,diagnostics,diag,link,unlink,claim,comment,attach,attachments,attach-rm,complete,edit,block,schedule,unblock,promote,archive,tail,dispatch,daemon,watch,stats,notify-subscribe,notify-list,notify-unsubscribe,log,runs,heartbeat,assignees,context,specify,decompose,gc}
                     ...

Durable SQLite-backed task board shared across Hermes profiles. Tasks are
claimed atomically, can depend on other tasks, and are executed by a named
profile in an isolated workspace. See https://hermes-
agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/kanban or docs/hermes-
kanban-v1-spec.pdf for the full design.

positional arguments:
  {init,boards,create,swarm,list,ls,show,assign,reclaim,reassign,diagnostics,diag,link,unlink,claim,comment,attach,attachments,attach-rm,complete,edit,block,schedule,unblock,promote,archive,tail,dispatch,daemon,watch,stats,notify-subscribe,notify-list,notify-unsubscribe,log,runs,heartbeat,assignees,context,specify,decompose,gc}
    init                Create kanban.db if missing (idempotent)
    boards              Manage kanban boards (one board per project /
                        workstream)
    create              Create a new task
    swarm               Create a Kanban Swarm v1 graph (parallel workers →
                        verifier → synthesizer)
    list (ls)           List tasks
    show                Show a task with comments + events
    assign              Assign or reassign a task
    reclaim             Release an active worker claim on a running task
    reassign            Reassign a task to a different profile, optionally
                        reclaiming first
    diagnostics (diag)  List active diagnostics on the current board
    link                Add a parent->child dependency
    unlink              Remove a parent->child dependency
    claim               Atomically claim a ready task (prints resolved
                        workspace path)
    comment             Append a comment
    attach              Attach a local file to a task
    attachments         List a task's attachments
    attach-rm           Delete an attachment by id
    complete            Mark one or more tasks done
    edit                Edit recovery fields on an already-completed task
    block               Mark one or more tasks blocked
    schedule            Park one or more tasks in Scheduled (waiting on time,
                        not human input)
    unblock             Return blocked/scheduled tasks to ready, or todo while
                        parents remain open

#!/bin/bash
# VR-10 per-mutant interruption-safe supervisor for T1 Rework7-A.
#
# One mutant per foreground invocation, well under the 600 s lane limit.
#
# Interruption safety contract (recovery packet SS5.4):
#   * a FRESH backup is verified before anything is touched;
#   * the EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP restoration trap is installed BEFORE the mutation;
#   * on any exit path the trap terminates and REAPS the test process group
#     FIRST, then restores the file UNCONDITIONALLY second;
#   * the restore is verified by sha256 + size + mtime + cmp;
#   * a restoration failure OVERRIDES the recorded status.
# No Python `finally` is relied on for process-group termination anywhere.

set -u

ROOT=/Users/vladmihaimiron/Documents/DebateAIRO/dialectical-engine
SCRATCH=/tmp/t1r7
LOGDIR="$ROOT/docs/missions/2026-08-17-accounts-privacy-security/logs"
PREFIX="T1-rework7-vr10r2"

MUT_ID="${1:?usage: vr10-supervisor.sh <MUTANT-ID>}"
SHORT="${MUT_ID%%-*}"                       # e.g. M01
# RECEIPT_TAG scopes the receipt names so no invocation can ever overwrite
# another one's log or status. Unset => the plain per-mutant verdict receipt.
TAG="${RECEIPT_TAG:-}"
BASE="$PREFIX-$(echo "$SHORT" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')${TAG:+-$TAG}"
LOG="$LOGDIR/$BASE.log"
STAT="$LOGDIR/$BASE.status"

REG="$ROOT/apps/api/src/registration.ts"
MAIN="$ROOT/apps/api/src/main.ts"
POL="$ROOT/packages/register/src/auth-policy.ts"

# string would also match the shell that is running this script, because this
# script's own text mentions vitest.
live_vitest() {
  pgrep -f vitest 2>/dev/null | while read -r p; do
    cmd=$(ps -o command= -p "$p" 2>/dev/null)
    case "$cmd" in
      *zsh*|*bash*|*pgrep*|*/ps\ *) continue ;;
    esac
    case "$cmd" in

    esac
  done | tr '\n' ' '
}

sha()   { shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }
sizeof(){ wc -c < "$1" | tr -d ' '; }
mtime() { stat -f %m "$1"; }

  if [ -n "$TESTPID" ]; then
    if kill -0 "$TESTPID" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "CLEANUP: TERM to test process group -$TESTPID" >> "$LOG"
      kill -TERM -"$TESTPID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$TESTPID" 2>/dev/null

    r_sz=$(sizeof "$TARGET"); b_sz=$(sizeof "$BACKUP")
    r_mt=$(mtime "$TARGET");  b_mt=$(mtime "$BACKUP")
    if cmp -s "$BACKUP" "$TARGET"; then cmp_ok=IDENTICAL; else cmp_ok=DIFFERS; fi
    {
      echo "--- restoration ---"
      echo "restored_sha256 = $r_sha"
      echo "backup_sha256   = $b_sha"
      echo "restored_size   = $r_sz   backup_size  = $b_sz"
      echo "restored_mtime  = $r_mt   backup_mtime = $b_mt"
      echo "cmp             = $cmp_ok"
    } >> "$LOG"

    printf '%s\n' "RESTORE_FAILED_${MUT_ID}" > "$STAT"
    echo "EXIT=RESTORE_FAILED (status overridden; gate status was $GATE_STATUS)" >> "$LOG"

fi
say "preflight_live_vitest=NONE"

p_reg=$(sha "$REG"); p_main=$(sha "$MAIN"); p_pol=$(sha "$POL")
say "pre_sha256_registration_ts=$p_reg"
say "pre_sha256_main_ts=$p_main"
say "pre_sha256_auth_policy_ts=$p_pol"
if [ "$p_reg" != "$REG_REQ" ] || [ "$p_main" != "$MAIN_REQ" ] || [ "$p_pol" != "$POL_REQ" ]; then
  say "ABORT: candidate drift before $MUT_ID"
  printf '%s\n' "ABORT_CANDIDATE_DRIFT" > "$STAT"; exit 92
fi
say "preflight_candidate=ALL-3-MATCH"

# ------------------------------------------------- fresh verified backup ----
case "$MUT_ID" in
  *) TARGET_KEY=$(python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/t1r7'); import mutspec
print(next(m[1] for m in mutspec.MUTANTS if m[0]=='$MUT_ID'))") ;;
esac
case "$TARGET_KEY" in
  registration) TARGET="$REG";  BACKUP="$SCRATCH/registration.baseline.ts" ;;
  main)         TARGET="$MAIN"; BACKUP="$SCRATCH/main.baseline.ts" ;;
  policy)       TARGET="$POL";  BACKUP="$SCRATCH/auth-policy.baseline.ts" ;;
  *) say "ABORT: unknown target key '$TARGET_KEY'"; printf '%s\n' "ABORT_TARGET" > "$STAT"; exit 93 ;;
esac

  printf '%s\n' "ABORT_FRESH_BACKUP" > "$STAT"; exit 94

  say "ABORT: mutation did not land cleanly (see log)"
  printf '%s\n' "ABORT_MUTATION" > "$STAT"; exit 95

# Build the gate as a real argv array so the -t filter keeps its quoting.
GATE_KIND=$(grep '^MUT_GATE_KIND=' "$LOG" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2-)

# candidate this selected block spends ~1.05 s total in tests (23/23 green), so
# the ceiling has ~10x headroom and never fires on candidate bytes — proved by
# the bounded-gate GREEN control receipts. Its only effect is to turn a mutant's
# infinite park into a crisp bounded failure with a real summary and raw status,
# instead of vitest force-terminating itself (143) with no summary at all.
case "$GATE_KIND" in
  UNIT) GATE=(node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/unit/registration.test.ts \
              -t 'T1 rework7' --testTimeout=10000) ;;
  ARCH) GATE=(node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/architecture/t1-argon2-worker-contract.test.ts \
              -t 'rework7|shutdown drains|clamp-absorption' --testTimeout=10000) ;;

  printf '%s\n' "ABORT_MUTATION_NOT_LANDED" > "$STAT"; exit 96

say "gate: $GATE_CMD"

TESTPID=$!

COMPILE_ERR=$(grep -cE "Transform failed|SyntaxError|Failed to load url|Error: Build failed|esbuild" "$LOG")

NUM_PASSED=$(echo "$SUMMARY"  | sed -n 's/.*[| ]\([0-9]*\) passed.*/\1/p')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply exactly ONE VR-10 mutant to the governed target file.

This process does the mutation and NOTHING else. It owns no restoration and
spawns no test child: restoration is owned entirely by the shell supervisor's
EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP trap, which is installed BEFORE this script is ever invoked.
That is the exact defect that contaminated the interrupted run — a Python
`finally` cannot survive the process being killed, so it is not used here.

Reads the mutation source from the candidate BACKUP (never from the working
tree), asserts each anchor matches exactly once, asserts the result differs,
writes the mutant, and prints machine-readable facts for the supervisor.
"""
import hashlib
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/t1r7")
import mutspec  # noqa: E402  (verbatim mutation table from the reviewed driver)


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("usage: apply_mutant.py <MUTANT-ID>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    wanted = sys.argv[1]

    row = next((m for m in mutspec.MUTANTS if m[0] == wanted), None)
    if row is None:
        print(f"ABORT: unknown mutant id {wanted}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    name, target, gate, edits = row

    path = mutspec.TARGETS[target]
    backup = mutspec.BACKUPS[target]

    # The working tree must already be at the candidate before we mutate it.
    if digest(path) != digest(backup):
        print(f"ABORT: {path} is not byte-identical to {backup} before {name}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    original = backup.read_text()
    mutated = original
    for old, new in edits:
        hits = mutated.count(old)
        if hits != 1:
            print(f"ABORT: {name} anchor matched {hits} times, expected 1", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        mutated = mutated.replace(old, new, 1)
    if mutated == original:
        print(f"ABORT: {name} produced no change", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    path.write_text(mutated)

    gate_kind = "UNIT" if gate is mutspec.UNIT else "ARCH"
    print(f"MUT_NAME={name}")
    print(f"MUT_TARGET_PATH={path}")
    print(f"MUT_BACKUP_PATH={backup}")
    print(f"MUT_GATE_KIND={gate_kind}")
    print(f"MUT_GATE_CMD={' '.join(gate)}")
    print(f"MUT_EDITS={len(edits)}")
    print(f"MUT_SHA={digest(path)}")
    print(f"MUT_SIZE={path.stat().st_size}")
    return 0


sys.exit(main())

#   * ONE mutant per foreground invocation, well under the 600 s lane limit;
#   * a FRESH backup is verified before anything is touched;
#   * the EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP restoration trap is installed BEFORE the mutation;
#   * on any exit path the trap terminates and REAPS the test process group
#     FIRST, then restores the file UNCONDITIONALLY second;
#   * the restore is verified by sha256 + size + mtime + cmp;
#   * a restoration failure OVERRIDES the recorded status;
#   * RECEIPT_TAG makes every receipt name unique, so no invocation can ever
#     overwrite another's log or status.
# No Python `finally` is relied on for process-group termination anywhere.
# No background driver exists and no two mutants ever overlap.

T1 Rework8 is complete. All four binding findings are repaired and proven, every gate this seat can hold is green, and the one gate it provably cannot hold is handed back intact.

**What was wrong and what fixed it**

- **F1** — `cancel()` is a no-op once the KDF is dispatched, so the reservation-rejection continuation released the admission token while the password was still live in the pool. Hash work now exposes a `settlement` promise that resolves only when the work is genuinely finished; both continuation arms await it before releasing. Drain can no longer walk past secret-bearing work.
- **F2** — the password lives in a start *closure*, which `retainedStateContains` can never enter, so queued cancellation was unprovable. Added an observable `registrationPasswordReferencesHeld` counter plus a test that saturates all 32 hash slots before queuing the target.
- **F3** — the retired M15 mutated the occupancy *readout*; it is replaced by a mutation of the real acquisition predicate, with the readout deliberately untouched so every failure comes from enforcement.
- **F4** — `registration_28s_margin_ms` (~10.1 s, positive) and `shared_18s_diagnostic_margin_ms` (~0.1 s) are now named for the deadlines they actually measure. No threshold or runtime deadline changed.

**Evidence** — RED-1/2/3 all reproduced on entry product bytes with crisp assertions (RED-3 on real PostgreSQL showed the mislabel as exactly the 10,000 ms deadline gap). VR-10: 17 mutants, 17 killed, 0 survivors, 17 byte-exact restores, 0 timeout-only kills. Final gates: unit 26/26, architecture 68/68, three identical fresh capacity repeats with zero drift, typecheck/lint/diff-check all 0.

Two judgment calls worth flagging: the first M15 sweep killed the mutant but let the three gated 104th tests fail as bare *timeouts*, which F3 forbids as evidence — I strengthened those tests with a scheduler-turn race (no wall clock, nothing removed) and re-ran the whole sweep on the final bytes. Both the superseded and authoritative receipts are on disk. Separately, `main.ts`, `auth-policy.ts` and four other governed paths show as modified in `git status`; the manifest check confirms all nine are byte-identical to entry — that dirt was inherited and untouched.

Exactly three allowlisted paths changed. HEAD unchanged, index empty, nothing staged or committed, no children alive.

The Rework7 Router full-file receipt is invalidated by these byte changes. Router must run once, in the sole controlled visible lane, on these exact bytes:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/integration/registration-database.test.ts
```

It measures ~25 minutes against this lane's 600 s cap, so it was not attempted and no substitute was run.

ROUTER FULL SUITE REQUIRED
